rendered: The review does not recommend this. It argues against it. Recovering current collectors such as copper and aluminium is described as critical because copper smelting is a key contributor to SOx and other greenhouse gas emissions in the cradle-to-gate stages of the battery life cycle. From that, the review concludes that dissolving aluminium in an alkaline solution is not a sustainable separation method[1]. For separating cathode coatings from aluminium foil, the review instead points to ethylene glycol, which has been used to delaminate cathode films from Al foil in seconds[2], though it does not remove the PVDF binder.
